sections.html:
A cash sale to a buyer who takes the building as is gets you out quickest in Union City, because the buyer absorbs the city's sale-of-property letter and any repair list. Listing with an agent can still bring a strong price for a clean two-family or a condo, and owners may sell on their own, but every path ends at the Building Department for the same letter.

The city has an estimated 66,656 residents in mid-2025, all on 1.29 square miles of land. It sits on the Palisades ridge in northern Hudson County, and streets run on a numbered grid.

The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $471,600 and median gross rent is $1,537. Only 19.1 percent of the city's 25,725 households own their home, so most buildings are rented and a typical seller owns a two- to six-family house or a condo. Owners with a mortgage carry a median of $3,088 a month in housing costs, and median household income is $64,310.

About 81.8 percent of residents age five and over speak a language other than English at home, and the city posts its forms in English and Spanish. Listing material in both languages reaches more buyers. Translate the key disclosures too, so a buyer and the buyer's family can read what they are signing.

Union City asks for a Sale of Property letter from the Building Department before a sale. The application form names the owner, buyer, building type and number of units, and a mandatory lead inspection must be completed before the letter is issued. The letter is good for 60 days after issuance, so a seller who is slow to close may need to renew.

Sale of Property letter costs and rules
Letter detailAmount or rule
Sale of Property letter processing$100
Lead inspection, 1 to 4 units$120 per unit
Lead inspection, 5 or more units$220 per unit

Duplicate tax bill$5

Ask the Building Department to confirm what applies to your building when you apply.

sections.h2: Other Building Department forms and basement apartments
sections.html:
The Building Department also posts a Certificate of Occupancy Exemption Letter, an Application for Inspection Approval Certificate, a Certification of Continued Use form and a procedure for legalizing non-conforming basement units. A basement apartment that was never permitted is the item that most often slows a Union City closing, so ask what it will take to legalize or remove one before you list.

A house with an unpermitted basement unit can still sell, usually to a cash buyer, but open issues can delay the sale letter.

The city's forms page lists a rent control program with an annual registration statement, a legal rent request form, capital improvement and hardship applications, and a landlord and tenant inquiry form. The program applies to covered rental units, so the buyer takes the building with its registration and legal rents. Gather the annual registration statement and the legal rent for each unit early.

Other filings come up in the same transaction.

  • A registration form for multiple dwellings and a Multiple Dwelling Green Card.
  • A Landlord Identity Statement filed with the City Clerk.
  • A registration of vacant and abandoned properties, and a separate registration form for properties in foreclosure.
  • A request form for a rebuild letter after a fire or similar loss.

An empty building is not a simple exit. If you hold a vacant house, ask the Building Department which registrations apply before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: How the lead inspection fits in
sections.html:
The lead inspection is not optional. The city will not issue the Sale of Property letter until it is complete, and the form lists the per-unit fee right under the lead inspection note. A two-family house pays for two units and a six-family building for six, so count units the same way the city does before you budget.

Book the inspection as soon as you have a contract, since the letter's 60 day clock only starts once the letter is issued. Booking late means the inspection, not the paperwork, becomes the bottleneck. If the inspection finds a problem, ask the Building Department what has to be corrected before it releases the letter.

Bergenline Avenue is the main shopping street and the main bus corridor. Route 495 leads to the Lincoln Tunnel, and the Hudson-Bergen Light Rail stops at 49th Street near the West New York and North Bergen lines. New Jersey Transit buses run to the Port Authority Bus Terminal in Midtown Manhattan, the George Washington Bridge Bus Terminal and Jersey City. Buyers who commute into New York weigh these links heavily, so mention them in a listing.

The city bills in quarters due on February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. Overdue amounts carry interest of 8% a year up to $1,500 and 18% a year above that, and the city allows 10 calendar days from the original due date only if bills were mailed on time. A municipal lien still unpaid on November 11 can go to tax sale, and anything in lien must be paid with certified funds.

The Tax Department site carries a reassessment presentation and FAQ in English and Spanish, a state revaluation order, an assessment lookup and instructions for appealing a property value. Senior Freeze applications and a 5 Year Tax Abatement application are posted there too. Taxes owed at closing come out of the seller's proceeds, so ask for the exact balance a few days ahead. Hand the new owner the current tax bill at closing and ask the department for a duplicate if you cannot find it.

Because most Union City sales involve multi-unit buildings, buyers and their attorneys ask for more paperwork than they would on a single-family house.

  • The unit count and building type for the sale letter application.
  • Proof the lead inspection is booked or complete.
  • The rent control registration and legal rent for each unit.
  • Any open basement or conversion issues, and the legalization steps.
  • The current tax bill and the status of each quarter.

Plan the calendar around the 60 day window. If the closing slips, you may need to renew the letter. A cash buyer can often work within that window, though the same items still apply.

faqs.q: What letter does Union City require to sell a house?
faqs.a: A Sale of Property letter from the Building Department, which costs $100 to process and requires a mandatory lead inspection first. The letter is good for 60 days after issuance.

faqs.q: How much is the lead inspection in Union City?
faqs.a: The city's sale-of-property form lists $120 per unit for one to four units and $220 per unit for five or more. Ask the Building Department to confirm what applies to your building when you apply.

faqs.q: What are the Union City tax due dates?
faqs.a: Taxes are due on the first of February, May, August and November. Interest is 8% up to $1,500 of delinquency and 18% on the amount above that.

faqs.q: Does rent control follow the building when I sell in Union City?
faqs.a: Yes for covered rental units. The buyer takes the building with its registration and legal rents, so gather the annual registration statement and legal rent records before you list.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Union City house with an unpermitted basement apartment?
faqs.a: It can sell, usually to a cash buyer, but the Building Department publishes a procedure for legalizing non-conforming basement units and open issues can delay the sale letter. Ask the department what applies to your building before you go to market.
